# Node Graph Viewer

> Single-file web app that draws node graphs from text or JSON. Built for AI agents and humans.
> Machine-readable API description: the <script id="ngv-manifest"> block in index.html, or window.NodeGraph.describe().

## Fastest ways to show a graph

1. Share link (no clicks needed). Open one of:
   - index.html#b=<base64url(utf8 graph)>        (plain base64url; easiest to generate)
   - index.html#g=<base64url(deflate-raw(utf8))> (compressed; use NodeGraph.shareLink(graph))
   - index.html#t=<encodeURIComponent(graph text)>
   - index.html?src=<url of a CORS-enabled raw .json/.txt>
   Add ?embed=1 for a graph-only view (no input pane/toolbar) and ?template=<name> to pick a node library.
2. JavaScript (browser-driving agents): window.NodeGraph.load(jsonOrText, {template})
3. iframe: parent.postMessage({type:"load", id:1, graph}, "*") -> reply {ngv:true, for:"load", id:1, nodes, edges, warnings}
4. UI: paste into textarea#src. It redraws ~0.5 s after input; button#draw forces it.

## JavaScript API (window.NodeGraph)

- load(graph, {template, relayout=true, persist=false, tab}) -> {ok, nodes, edges, parameters, warnings, template}
- validate(graph) -> {ok, nodes, edges, warnings}      (parses without drawing)
- getGraph() -> JSON object of the drawn graph (same as the JSON button)
- getText(), getWarnings(), templates(), setTemplate(name), reference(), fit(), relayout()
- exportSVG() -> standalone SVG string with styles inlined
- encode(graph), shareLink(graph, {embed, template}) -> Promise<string>
- describe() -> the manifest

Loaded graphs do not overwrite the user's saved text (persist=false) until they edit or press Draw.

## Verifying your own output without seeing the page

After drawing, read: document.body.dataset.nodes / edges / warnings, the text of #warn, or call NodeGraph.getWarnings().
"Parsed OK." in #warn means zero warnings. Wait for body[data-ngv-ready="1"] before calling the API.

## Input format (text)

    # comments start with # or //
    param id "Label": type = default {min: 0, max: 1}        types: float int bool vector2 vector3 vector4 color texture string
    id "Label" {Setting: Value}: In, In=default -> Out, Out
    id.Port -> id.Port          (a parameter can be wired as:  paramId -> node.Port)

- id: no spaces or dots. Port names may contain spaces and must match exactly.
- Inputs left of ->, outputs right. Name=value sets a default shown while unconnected.
- A node used only in connections is auto-created. With a template selected, declare by type: m1 "Multiply".
- Each input should have at most one connection (else a warning). For multi-input sockets use numbered ports ("Geometry 1", "Geometry 2").

## Input format (JSON) - must start with "{"; schema: graph.schema.json

    {"parameters":[{"id":"dmg","label":"Damage","type":"float","value":0,"props":{"min":0,"max":1}}],
     "nodes":[{"id":"mul","label":"Multiply","props":{"Mode":"Default"},"inputs":["A",{"name":"B","value":0.5}],"outputs":["Out"]},
              {"id":"add","type":"Add"}],
     "edges":[["dmg","mul.B"],["mul.Out","add.A"]]}

- {"id","type"} only: ports come from the active template.
- Edges are ["from.Port","to.Port"] ("from" may be just a parameter id). {from,to} objects also work.

## Templates

Built in: Unity Shader Graph, Blender Geometry Nodes, Blender Shader Nodes, Material Maker. NodeGraph.reference() returns the exact
node/port names for the active template; use them verbatim.
